_comment: Expected publication outcome per basket name for the pre-deploy gate (scripts/valuation_canary_summary.py --expect). Change an entry only together with the engine change that explains it, and say why here. 2026-09-27: calibrated premium (3.24%) is the default. 2026-10-02: a sound model that well-covered analysts do not back is published with a confidence alert (FLAGGED) instead of withheld; WITHHELD now means the model itself supports no single value (a failed or contradicting method, stale statements, a method the company does not fit) and the answer is the range. 2026-11-19: TSLA moves to WITHHELD under the unconfirmed-outlier rule (2026-11-18); other DCF-only names far outside every analyst target would move the same way, so run the canary before release. 2026-11-19 (canary run old vs new, Duke job 13865086): AMD, PYPL, TEX also move to WITHHELD under the same rule; valuations unchanged for all 17. A healthy engine now publishes about 9-10 of 17, so the nightly floor is 0.41. 2026-11-19 (production host, live vs candidate same time): NVDA, META, SNDK updated to today's outcome, identical on the live worker (data drift).

NVDA.why: Data drift, not an engine change: on 2026-11-19 the live worker (sha256:aa4948af) and the candidate gave this same outcome side by side on the production host. DCF about +148% vs the Street's +69% (55 analysts): published with a confidence alert because the Street covers less than the model's gap. Was PUBLISHED.

MSFT.why: DCF about +14% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+12%) corroborates if it lands above 15%.

META.why: Data drift, not an engine change: on 2026-11-19 the live worker (sha256:aa4948af) and the candidate gave this same outcome side by side on the production host. DCF about +73% vs the Street's +42%: the Street now covers enough of the gap to publish without an alert. Was FLAGGED.

GOOGL.why: DCF about +15% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+25%) corroborates if it lands above 15%.

CRH.why: DCF about +25% with the calibrated premium; the Street (+57%) corroborates.

TSLA.why: Since 2026-11-18 a cash-flow model with no second method, more than 10% outside every current target of at least 5 analysts, is a scenario, not a rating (valuation_methodology.withhold_unconfirmed_outlier). Tesla's DCF (about $20) sits far below the lowest of ~40 targets (about $128). Range only. Was FLAGGED.

AMD.why: Since 2026-11-19, range only under the unconfirmed-outlier rule (2026-11-18): a cash-flow model with no second method, more than 10% outside every current target of at least 5 analysts, is a scenario, not a rating. AMD's DCF (about $200-223) sits far below the price (about $488) and below every one of ~49 targets (mean about $658). Was FLAGGED.

AAPL.why: DCF-only, about -38% vs market; Street at the market. Published with a confidence alert since 2026-10-02 (was withheld).

AMZN.why: DCF about -29% vs market while the Street is +31%: model and Street point opposite ways, so it publishes with a confidence alert whenever its statements are current. Range only while they are not. On 2026-10-02 the provider had Amazon's June-2026 income statement but no balance sheet or cash flow for that quarter, so the last complete quarter (2026-03-31) was past the 150-day limit and the annual filing (2025-12-31) past the 200-day limit. The engine before 2026-10-02 carried the same statements blocker behind its Street reason, where a reader of the first sentence never saw it; the first pre-deploy gate run found it.

PYPL.why: Since 2026-11-19, range only under the unconfirmed-outlier rule (2026-11-18): a cash-flow model with no second method, more than 10% outside every current target of at least 5 analysts, is a scenario, not a rating. PayPal's DCF (about $96-124) sits far above the price (about $56) and above every one of ~33 targets (mean about $57). Was FLAGGED.

MC.PA.why: Latest annual filing beyond the 200-day limit and no semiannual bridge. Range only: stale statements are a model input problem, not a disagreement with the Street.

PCJEWELLER.NS.why: Perpetual DCF is negative; a failed leg never publishes. Range only.

MU.why: Memory maker valued mid-cycle: the Street's two covered years, then revenue back to trend and a 21% DRAM through-cycle operating margin. Far below the price while the Street sits above it, so published with a confidence alert.

GM.why: GM Financial is a consolidated captive lender; scenario only until an operating/finance split exists. Range only.

TEX.why: Since 2026-11-19, range only under the unconfirmed-outlier rule (2026-11-18): a cash-flow model with no second method, more than 10% outside every current target of at least 5 analysts, is a scenario, not a rating. Terex's DCF (about $94-119) sits about +100% above the price (about $53) and above every one of ~13 targets (mean about $74). Was PUBLISHED (borderline).

BKNG.why: Reports no cost of revenue in any year (expenses by function). It must build and pass integrity: before 2026-09-27 every Booking model failed the historical-period check, and payables measured against the absent line were projected at zero. Any publication outcome is accepted because the methods span right at the 1.8x limit: DCF about +34%, comps about +134% on Airbnb, Hilton and Royal Caribbean at 26.7x EBITDA versus Booking's own 12.2x. When the methods land inside the limit the value publishes, flagged if the Street does not back it.

SNDK.why: Data drift, not an engine change: on 2026-11-19 the live worker (sha256:aa4948af) and the candidate gave this same outcome side by side on the production host. Mid-cycle value about at the price (gap about 0%), so no alert. Was FLAGGED.
